about: Shakti Pumps is an Indian manufacturer of submersible pumps, motors and solar pumping systems based in Pithampur near Dhar, Madhya Pradesh. It sells to farmers, government programmes and infrastructure customers in India and exports to dozens of countries; solar pumps under agriculture subsidy schemes are a major part of its revenue. It is listed on NSE and BSE and has annual revenue of more than 10 billion rupees. It has regional brand awareness among Indian farmers.

Tesmec is an Italian company based in Milan that makes machinery and systems for building and maintaining power lines, fibre and gas pipelines, including trenchers, stringing equipment and railway-line monitoring and electrification systems. It operates in three segments, Energy, Trencher and Rail, and is listed on Euronext Milan STAR (TES). Customers are utilities, contractors and rail operators. It is a B2B industrial brand known in infrastructure circles, with little consumer visibility.

Lakeland Industries is an Alabama-based maker of protective clothing for industrial workers, firefighters and first responders, including chemical suits, disposable coveralls and flame-resistant garments. Its customers are industrial companies, distributors and governments in the United States and abroad, with factories in Mexico, China, Vietnam and other countries. Founded in 1982 and listed on Nasdaq (LAKE), it has revenue around US$130 million. It is a B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Steel Exchange India is a Visakhapatnam-based steel manufacturer in Andhra Pradesh, producing TMT rebars, wire rods and structural steel from its integrated plant, and selling to construction and infrastructure customers. It is listed on the BSE and NSE and sells under the SEIL brand. Its customers are builders and distributors across southern India. It has regional brand recognition in Indian construction materials but is small by industry standards.

Crossject is a Dijon-based French specialty pharmaceutical company developing needle-free auto-injectors, notably Zeneo, with products such as Zeneo Midazolam for seizure emergencies and an adrenaline version, with US BARDA funding. It is listed on Euronext Paris (ALCJ). Customers are healthcare systems, military and emergency users. It is a small niche medical device firm with limited public awareness and revenue dependent on grants and early product sales.

Tasmea is a Perth-based Australian industrial services group, listed on the ASX (TEA), that grows by acquiring specialist engineering, maintenance and technical service companies, for mining, energy and infrastructure customers. It earns revenue from services to resource and industrial clients in Australia. It is a B2B group with low consumer brand awareness, and its growth story depends on acquisitions of small companies.

Israeli regenerative medicine company that develops recombinant human collagen produced in genetically engineered tobacco plants, using it for tissue repair, bioinks for 3D bioprinting of breast implants and organs, and dermal fillers. Its main collaboration is with AbbVie (Allergan) on a dermal filler programme, with milestone payments providing income. Based in Rehovot, Israel, and listed on Nasdaq (CLGN) and the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. B2B biotech, with no consumer brand, and minimal public awareness outside medical aesthetics and biotech investors.

South Korean manufacturer of atomic force microscopes and nanometrology equipment used by semiconductor makers, research labs and universities, one of the leading suppliers in the field. Founded in 1997, based in Suwon, it is listed on KOSDAQ (140860) and sells to chipmakers such as Samsung, SK Hynix and global labs, with subsidiaries in the US, Europe, Japan and Singapore. Revenue comes from instrument sales and service. B2B with strong niche reputation in scientific instrumentation but no consumer brand profile.

South Korean manufacturer of power cables, industrial wires and communication cables, supplying utilities, construction, telecoms and industrial customers in Korea and exports. Based in Seoul, it is listed on the Korea Exchange (006340). It is an established mid-sized cable maker, benefiting from grid and construction demand. Revenue comes from sales of low and medium voltage cable, wire and related products to contractors and utilities. B2B with little consumer brand visibility.

Swedish shop fitting company that designs, manufactures and installs shelving, checkouts, lighting and fixtures for supermarkets, fashion chains, convenience stores and other retailers across Europe. Based in Jonkoping and part of ITAB Group, listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. Customers are large retail chains and store developers, and revenue comes from project-based store fit-outs. B2B, with no consumer brand awareness, although its work is visible in stores.

Glass container manufacturer based in Valdosta, Georgia, producing premium glass bottles for spirits, wine and other beverage brands, as well as jars for food. It is a US operation linked to Yamamura Glass of Japan and serves liquor and beverage brand owners that want high-end packaging. Revenue is from bottle sales under supply contracts. B2B with no consumer brand awareness, although its bottles reach shelves under customers' brands.

B2B component supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Subsidiary of South Korea's SKC that manufactures glass substrates for advanced semiconductor packaging, targeting AI and high-performance computing chips that need finer interconnects than organic substrates. Based in Covington, Georgia, where it built a plant supported by US CHIPS Act funding and where Applied Materials is a partner, it sells to chipmakers and packaging firms. It is an early-stage supplier ramping production. B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

US solar manufacturer that made cylindrical thin-film CIGS photovoltaic tubes designed for commercial rooftops, built a factory in Fremont, California and received a 535 million dollar US Department of Energy loan guarantee. Falling silicon panel prices undermined its economics and it filed for bankruptcy in September 2011, a widely covered political controversy in Washington. Defunct, so no sponsorship potential, though the name is still recognised in cleantech and politics.

Chinese commercial property company in Shanghai that develops business parks and suburban office space, according to its Crunchbase line. Respected B2B name in the CRO industry; consumers do not know it.

Customers include appliance makers and electronics manufacturers across Europe.

about: Indian railway wagon and rolling stock manufacturer in Kolkata, producing freight wagons, brake systems and related components for Indian Railways, private freight operators and industrial customers, with growth driven by railway modernisation. Plants are in Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal, with a joint venture with a Russian partner on wagons. Listed on NSE and BSE. Known to railway procurement and investors, with no consumer brand.

Swedish steel and metals service company in Malmo that distributes and processes steel, stainless steel and aluminium, supplying manufacturers, construction firms and machine builders, mainly in Sweden, Finland, Germany and Poland. Revenue comes from product sales and processing services, so it follows industrial demand. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (BEGR). Industrial B2B brand known to Nordic customers, with no consumer awareness.

US semiconductor company in Chandler, Arizona, and a leading maker of magnetoresistive RAM (MRAM), a non-volatile memory used in industrial automation, data centres, automotive and aerospace systems that need fast, durable storage. Customers are electronics manufacturers worldwide. It was spun out of Freescale in 2008 and listed on Nasdaq (MRAM). B2B component brand known to engineers, with no consumer awareness.

Jyoti CNC Automation is an Indian maker of computer numerical control (CNC) machine tools, including turning centres, vertical and horizontal machining centres and multi-axis machines, sold under the Jyoti and Hi-Tech brands. Customers are industrial manufacturers in automotive, aerospace, defence, medical and general engineering, and revenue comes from machine sales, spares and service. Founded in 1991 and operating from Rajkot, Gujarat, one of Asia's larger CNC makers, with exports to Europe, North America and Asia and a European subsidiary in Germany/France. Listed on Indian exchanges (NSE/BSE: JYOTICNC) after a 2024 IPO. B2B industrial brand, with low public awareness but strong standing within manufacturing.

Toyo Solar, a Vietnam-based subsidiary of the Japanese-owned Toyo Co., Ltd., manufactures solar cells and modules at a large plant in Quang Ninh province, exporting mainly to the United States market. Its products are high-efficiency crystalline silicon cells and modules for utility-scale and commercial solar projects, sold B2B to developers and module assemblers. Toyo Co. is listed on Nasdaq (TOYO), having gone public via a 2024 IPO. Part of the global shift of solar manufacturing out of China into Southeast Asia, with multi-gigawatt capacity. B2B manufacturer with no consumer brand, so limited sponsorship use beyond energy-transition messaging.

Buhler Industries is a Canadian agricultural equipment maker, based in Winnipeg, producing tractors under the Versatile brand (four-wheel-drive articulated tractors for large farms), plus sprayers, swathers and other implements, with Farm King and Allied attachments. It sells to farmers through a dealer network in North America, and also supplies tractors internationally. Owned by Russian farm machinery group Rostselmash from 2007. A recognised farm-machinery brand in North America, but sales run through dealers and its audience is agricultural, with low general consumer reach.

Chargeurs is a French industrial and luxury-linked group that was founded in 1872 and is listed on Euronext Paris. It runs several businesses: Chargeurs Protective Films (surface protection films for metals and plastics), Chargeurs Fashion Technologies (interlinings used by apparel makers), Chargeurs Luxury Materials (wool top for luxury suiting, via the Leach and Lainière de Picardie operations) and PCC Chargeurs Museum Solutions. Customers are manufacturers and luxury brands, with revenue of about 700 million euros and operations globally. B2B supplier with little consumer brand awareness, though the luxury link may appeal to some partners.

Glaston is a Finnish technology company making glass processing machines, especially for tempering, laminating and bending architectural, automotive and appliance glass, and offers upgrades, spare parts and service plus software. Its customers are glass processors serving construction, automotive and solar. It operates in Europe, North America and Asia, has several hundred employees, and revenue of roughly 200 million euros. Listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (GLA1V), with a history linked to the Finnish Tamglass business. B2B equipment maker with little consumer awareness, so its sponsorship relevance is limited.

Hi-Tech Pipes is an Indian maker of steel pipes and tubes, including electric resistance welded pipes, galvanised pipes, structural hollow sections and solar mounting structures, with plants in several Indian states. It sells to construction, infrastructure, automotive, agriculture and engineering customers via distributors, and generates revenue from steel product sales. Based in the Delhi region, it is listed on BSE and NSE (HITECH). B2B industrial brand with minimal consumer recognition, mostly known in Indian trade channels.

Luoyang Northglass Technology is a Chinese glass processing and equipment company in Luoyang, Henan, known for glass deep-processing machinery such as tempering furnaces, laminating lines and related equipment and services for architectural and industrial glass makers. Customers are glass processors in China and export markets. It is listed on a mainland Chinese exchange and grew out of a long-standing Chinese glass industry business. B2B equipment maker with no consumer brand awareness and very limited relevance for sponsorship.

Guerrilla RF is a US fabless semiconductor company designing radio-frequency (RF) and microwave chips such as low-noise amplifiers, power amplifiers and front-end modules, for wireless infrastructure, 5G, military, satellite, cellular boosters and IoT. Customers are electronics manufacturers and defence contractors, buying components designed in Greensboro. Listed on the OTC markets (GUER) after a reverse merger in 2021. Small company with revenue of a few tens of millions of dollars and almost no consumer brand awareness, so limited sponsorship relevance.

Neuromeka is a South Korean robotics company that makes collaborative robot arms (the Indy and Rainbow series) and robotic software and AI for factories, as well as the 'Neuromeka' automation solutions for tasks like machine tending, welding, and pharmaceutical and food lines. Customers are manufacturers and system integrators, and the company is based in Seoul with a plant in Korea. It listed on the Korean KOSDAQ market in 2024 (348340). A fast-growing B2B robotics brand with limited consumer awareness.

Pitti Engineering is an Indian engineering company in Hyderabad that makes electric motor components, including laminations, rotor and stator cores, die-cast rotors, machined components and fabricated assemblies, plus steel castings and forgings, for electric motor and generator makers, including wind turbine, railway, and traction customers. It exports to Europe and the US. Founded in 1983 and listed on BSE and NSE (PITTIENG). B2B industrial supplier with very little consumer brand awareness.

TeraView is a Cambridge, UK, company that makes terahertz imaging and spectroscopy equipment, which uses terahertz light to inspect materials, coatings, pharmaceuticals and semiconductor devices without damaging them. It spun out of Toshiba Research Europe and sells to pharmaceutical, semiconductor, industrial inspection and security customers, with products like TeraPulse and TeraPulse Lx. Private and venture-funded. Small B2B scientific instruments maker with niche recognition, little consumer awareness, and no sponsorship record I know of.

Confidence Group (Confidence Petroleum India) is a Nagpur-based Indian company in the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) business, bottling and distributing cooking gas cylinders, building LPG autogas stations and manufacturing cylinders and valves, with additional ventures in CNG and energy equipment. Customers are households, vehicle owners and industrial buyers across several Indian states. Listed on BSE and NSE (CONFIPET). It operates with a regional brand in LPG retail and has little recognition outside India.

Prosafe is a Norwegian offshore accommodation company, with semi-submersible rigs known as floatels that house workers beside oil and gas platforms, mostly in the North Sea and Brazil. Customers are oil companies and contractors, and it is based in Stavanger and listed on Oslo Bors (PRS). It restructured its debt in the early 2020s. B2B offshore service provider with no consumer profile, and little relevance for sponsorship.

Chinese warehouse robotics company headquartered in Beijing that makes autonomous mobile robots for goods-to-person picking, sorting and shelf-moving in logistics, for retailers, e-commerce companies and manufacturers, along with software to run robot fleets. Founded in 2015, it listed in Hong Kong in 2025 and serves hundreds of customers in dozens of countries. The record shows a Georgia address, which is its US operation. B2B industrial brand with low consumer awareness.

It describes itself as a global supplier of clear rigid packaging materials, with plants in Salalah, Oman and later sites in Europe and elsewhere, serving packaging converters and food and consumer goods firms in over 80 countries. Its output is among the world's largest in the segment. Based in Muscat, it is a private industrial group. B2B materials brand with little consumer visibility.

Founded in 1969, it has over 100 locations worldwide and annual sales above 3 billion dollars. Private-equity backed, with Oak Hill Capital and Investcorp among investors. B2B packaging brand with limited consumer awareness.

about: Markforged is a Waltham, Massachusetts maker of industrial 3D printers, best known for the Metal X system, which prints metal parts by bonding metal powder in plastic, and for carbon-fibre composite printers, with its Digital Forge software and cloud platform. Customers are manufacturers in aerospace, automotive, defence and tooling who print parts on demand, buying printers, materials and software subscriptions. Founded in 2013 by Greg Mark, it went public on the NYSE (MKFG) via a SPAC in 2021, with annual revenue of roughly 80 to 100 million dollars. Nano Dimension acquired it in 2025. B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

Virgin Hyperloop was a Los Angeles company developing a hyperloop passenger and cargo transport system, in which pods travel in low-pressure tubes at very high speed. It grew from Hyperloop One, and Richard Branson's Virgin Group became the lead investor in 2017, with DP World also a major backer. It ran a test track in Nevada and carried its first passengers in 2020, then dropped passenger plans to focus on cargo, cut most staff and shut down at the end of 2023. Funding was about 368 million dollars. The Virgin brand gave it high public visibility, though it never operated commercially.

Formlabs is a Somerville, Massachusetts maker of desktop and industrial 3D printers, best known for the Form series of resin printers (Form 3 and Form 4) and the Fuse series of SLS powder printers, together with materials and PreForm software. Customers include dentists, engineers, designers, manufacturers and universities, and it earns revenue from machines and recurring resin and materials sales. Founded in 2011 by MIT Media Lab alumni, it was valued at about 2 billion dollars in 2021 and has several hundred staff. Private. Well-known B2B brand in 3D printing, with moderate visibility among makers.

Jaka Robot is a Shanghai-based industrial robot maker founded in 2014 that specialises in collaborative robots, or cobots, which work safely beside people on factory lines, alongside SCARA and mobile robot platforms. Customers are electronics, automotive, logistics, medical and consumer goods manufacturers across China and export markets, buying robots, controllers and integration services. It has raised venture funding and has pursued a Shanghai STAR Market listing. Funding of about 235 million dollars. B2B industrial brand with little consumer awareness.

Customers are farmers, contractors and dealers. State-linked Weichai ownership and sales of several billion dollars. B2B machinery brand, known among farmers in China and emerging markets.

Founded in 2016, it raised about 194 million dollars from venture and institutional investors and entered insolvency proceedings in 2025. B2B logistics technology brand with limited public awareness outside supply chain circles.

Customers are hardware and robotics companies, automotive, aerospace and medical device firms, paying per order, with software for project management. Founded in 2013 by Dave Evans, it raised about 190 million dollars and was acquired in 2025 by Japanese industrial supplier MISUMI Group. B2B engineering brand with strong recognition among product engineers, none among consumers.

about: Fast Radius was a Chicago cloud manufacturing company that offered on-demand production of custom parts through 3D printing, injection moulding and CNC machining, with a digital platform that quoted designs and managed supply chains. Customers included industrial, automotive and consumer product companies such as automotive and consumer product firms. Founded in 2013, it went public via SPAC on Nasdaq (FSRD) in February 2022, raising about 168 million dollars in total funding, then filed for Chapter 11 in November 2022, with its assets bought by SyBridge Technologies. B2B manufacturing services brand with limited consumer awareness.

LIBERTY Steel Group is the steel and metals recycling arm of the GFG Alliance, the industrial group of Sanjeev Gupta, headquartered in London. It owned steelworks in the UK, Australia (Whyalla), Czechia, Poland, Romania and the US, producing long steel, rails and speciality products for construction, rail and manufacturing customers. It faced a liquidity crisis after the 2021 collapse of Greensill Capital, its main lender, and several units entered administration or liquidation, including the Whyalla works in 2025 and the UK business. B2B industrial brand with prominent regional profile in steel communities.

Cactus Wellhead is the operating business of Cactus Inc., a Houston, Texas manufacturer of wellheads and pressure control equipment, listed on the NYSE (WHD). Its products, including wellheads, frac trees and the SafeDrill rig-floor system, are used in drilling and completing oil and gas wells, mainly in the Permian and other US shale basins, and it also rents equipment and services. Founded in 2011 by Scott Bender, it manufactures in Bossier City, Louisiana and China, and formed a surface pressure control venture with Baker Hughes in 2025. Annual revenue of about 1 billion dollars. B2B oilfield brand with no consumer visibility.

MariMed is a Norwood, Massachusetts multi-state cannabis operator, listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange (MRMD) and traded over the counter in the US. It develops and manages cultivation and dispensary facilities for licensed operators, and sells its own brands, including Kalm Fusion, Betty's Eddies and Bubby's Baked, through licensed dispensaries in states such as Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts and Nevada. Revenue is around 150 million dollars. Customers are adult-use and medical cannabis consumers and licensed partners. Cannabis advertising limits mean low mainstream awareness, though its edibles brands are known among US customers.

L.K. Technology Holdings is a Hong Kong-listed machinery group, with operations based in the Kwai Tsing district of the New Territories, that makes plastic injection moulding machines and die-casting equipment through brands such as Chen Hsong and Chuan Lih Fa, plus related machinery distribution and parts. Customers are plastics, electronics, automotive and consumer product manufacturers in China and export markets, and revenue runs to hundreds of millions of dollars. Founded in 1986 and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (558). B2B machinery brand known among manufacturers in Asia, without consumer awareness.

Gunung Raja Paksi is an Indonesian steel producer based in Bekasi, West Java, listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (GGRP), making hot-rolled coils, H-beams, I-beams, rebar and other long and flat steel products for construction, infrastructure and manufacturing. It operates integrated steel mills with induction furnaces in the Greater Jakarta area, and also sells billets. Customers are builders, contractors and distributors in Indonesia, with annual sales of several hundred million dollars. It was founded in 1989. B2B industrial brand with solid recognition among Indonesian contractors but no consumer awareness.

Jai Balaji Industries is a Kolkata-based Indian steel and ferro alloy company listed on the NSE and BSE, producing sponge iron, pig iron, billets, TMT bars, wire rods, ductile iron pipes and ferroalloys at plants in West Bengal and elsewhere. Its brands include Jai Balaji TMT bars, sold to builders and infrastructure contractors through dealers in eastern India. It had a debt restructuring in earlier years and revenue of about 700 to 900 million dollars recently. B2B steel brand with solid awareness among builders in West Bengal and eastern India, but little national consumer recognition.

Steel Authority of India (SAIL) is a state-owned steel producer headquartered in New Delhi, listed on the NSE and BSE, and among India's largest, producing over 19 million tonnes of crude steel a year at integrated plants in Bhilai, Durgapur, Rourkela, Bokaro and Burnpur. It makes flat and long products, including plates, coils, rails, structurals and rebar, for construction, railways, automotive and defence customers. The Government of India holds a majority stake. Founded in 1973, it has roughly 60,000 employees. Strong B2B brand and high national recognition, including consumer-facing TMT bars.

Drilling Tools International is a Houston, Texas oilfield services company, listed on Nasdaq (DTI), that rents and sells downhole drilling tools such as drill pipe, stabilisers, motors and specialist equipment to oil and gas operators and drillers, with a growing manufacturing base and a 3D printing capability. Customers are US shale producers and service companies, with some international business. Founded in 1984 and public through a 2023 SPAC merger with ROC Energy Acquisition, it has about 600 employees and revenue of roughly 150 million dollars. Funding of about 41 million dollars. B2B oilfield brand with no consumer awareness.

Indian recycler of lead-acid batteries and other non-ferrous scrap, producing refined lead, lead alloys, aluminium alloys and plastic granules from recycled material. Founded in 1992, it runs plants across India and in Africa and elsewhere, including Senegal, Ghana, Mozambique, Tanzania, Sri Lanka and Oman, and sells to battery makers, auto and industrial manufacturers. Revenue is in the hundreds of millions of dollars and growing as it targets higher recycling capacity. Listed on the National Stock Exchange of India. B2B and sustainability story with little consumer awareness.

Chinese industrial equipment or automation manufacturer based in Quzhou, Zhejiang, listed on a Chinese exchange according to the funding record in yuan. The input places it among industrial and industrial automation businesses, selling to factories rather than consumers. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Japanese-origin automotive interior parts maker, supplying door trims, headliners and other interior components to car manufacturers, with an Indonesian plant serving the local auto industry in the Karawang manufacturing cluster. Customers are vehicle makers, so revenue depends on production volumes of Japanese brands in Southeast Asia. Parent is listed in Tokyo. B2B tier-one or tier-two supplier with no consumer brand recognition.

Premium packaging manufacturer for the beauty industry, making compacts, lipstick cases, mascara tubes, bottles and skincare containers for cosmetics and fragrance brands. It operates factories and design studios in Europe, the US and Asia and sells primarily to global beauty groups and indie brands. Founded in Spain, with HQ in Barcelona. B2B supplier, strong industry reputation but no consumer recognition.

Taiwanese industrial automation and semiconductor-related equipment business based in Taichung, which listed in the US via a special purpose acquisition vehicle. The input gives little detail on its exact products or customers. Likely a B2B equipment supplier serving electronics manufacturers in Taiwan and Asia. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Chinese electric two-wheeler and mobility business, selling electric bicycles and scooters and related services, and listed on Nasdaq as EZGO.
